questions.question: In a practical activity modelling natural selection, students pick up green and white cocktail sticks from green grass. What does this simple model demonstrate?
options: How camouflage affects an organism's chance of being caught by a predator
How organisms generate new mutations when they need them
How plants absorb nutrients from the soil using green pigment
How fast cocktail sticks can grow in different weather conditions

questions.question: Using the green and white cocktail stick model on green grass, what prediction can be made about the population of sticks left behind over several rounds of picking?
options: The percentage of white sticks remaining will increase over time
The percentage of green sticks remaining will increase over time
Both types of sticks will disappear at exactly the same rate
All green sticks will instantly transform into white sticks

questions.question: How would the outcome of the cocktail stick model change if the green grass became completely covered in white snow?
options: Green sticks would now be harder to see and survive better
White sticks would now be easier to see and picked first
White sticks would now be harder to see and survive better
Neither stick color would be visible to the predator at all

questions.question: Which term describes the special features that make an organism well suited to survive in its environment?
options: Adaptations
Habitats
Fossils
Nutrients

questions.question: A polar bear has a thick layer of blubber beneath its skin. How does this specific adaptation provide an advantage in its environment?
options: It helps the bear absorb light for photosynthesis
It provides thermal insulation to reduce heat loss in freezing temperatures
It allows the bear to run faster to catch flying birds
It makes the bear lighter so it can float on water easily

questions.question: Why do individual organisms in a habitat compete with one another?
options: Because resources in a habitat are limited
Because all organisms have identical genetic information
Because ecosystems require organisms to fight for entertainment
Because resources are unlimited and endlessly available

questions.question: Which set of resources are animals most likely to compete for in a woodland habitat?
options: Light, pollinators, carbon dioxide, and soil minerals
Food, water, space, shelter, and mates
Oxygen, rocks, sunshine, and seed dispersers
Temperature, wind direction, rainfall, and cloud cover

questions.question: In science, what is a 'scientific theory'?
options: An untested guess made by a single person without any evidence
A general explanation developed from evidence that explains many different examples
A set of strict rules that can never be modified or questioned
A prediction about the future that has no relationship to real-world observations

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how new advantageous features arise in a species during evolution?
options: Organisms decide to grow new features when the environment changes
New features appear randomly and are maintained if natural selection favours them
Evolution plans ahead to prepare organisms for future climate changes
Parents consciously pass on only their best trained physical traits

questions.question: If a weightlifter builds very large muscles through daily training, why is this change not considered evolution?
options: Because changes in an individual's features within its lifetime are not evolution
Because muscle growth is caused by genetic mutations in skin cells
Because physical exercise always decreases an organism's survival rate
Because evolution only occurs in plants and microorganisms, not animals

questions.question: What are fossils?
options: Dried leaves collected from living trees in modern forests
The mineralised remains or traces of once-living organisms
Fresh bones buried by animals a few days ago
Shells carved out of rock by ancient human sculptors

questions.question: Why are there limitations to the conclusions scientists can draw from the fossil record?
options: Soft-bodied organisms rarely form fossils, leaving gaps in the record
Fossils show exact videos of how ancient organisms behaved
Every single organism that ever lived has been preserved as a fossil
Fossils contain full intact DNA from billions of years ago

questions.question: A dog loses a leg in an accident. Why will its future puppies still be born with four legs?
options: Because environmental variation cannot be inherited by offspring
Because genetic variation changes whenever an injury occurs
Because the puppies choose how many legs to grow before birth
Because physical injuries are passed on through genetic instructions

questions.question: Which feature is an example of variation caused by genetic information?
options: A scar on a person's knee from falling off a bicycle
Camouflaged skin pattern on a chameleon
A tan gained by spending a week sitting in the sun
A dyed blue hairstyle

questions.question: In evolutionary biology, what does it mean when an individual is described as being 'fitter' or 'better adapted'?
options: It can run faster than any other species in the world
It has traits that give it a higher chance of surviving to reproduce in its environment
It spends more time exercising to build strong muscles
It is the largest and heaviest organism in the ecosystem

questions.question: What happens over several generations when an advantageous genetic feature helps individuals survive and reproduce?
options: The feature becomes more common in each generation of offspring
The feature completely disappears from the population
The feature is replaced by environmental injuries
The entire population immediately becomes extinct

questions.question: Based on scientific evidence, approximately how old is the Earth?
options: 4.5 million years old
4.5 billion years old
350 thousand years old
500 million years old

questions.question: According to scientific evidence, when did the first living organisms appear on Earth?
options: Around 3.8 billion years ago
Around 200 million years ago
Around 10 thousand years ago
Around 4.5 billion years ago

questions.question: Which of the following correctly orders the appearance of these life forms on Earth, from earliest to most recent?
options: Modern humans, first mammals, first land plants
First land plants, first mammals, modern humans
First mammals, modern humans, first land plants
Modern humans, first land plants, first mammals

questions.question: Why do scientists divide Earth's history into eons, periods, and epochs?
options: To make the huge span of Earth's history easier to understand and study
To calculate the exact date every single organism died
To prove that environmental variation is passed on to offspring
To track weather changes over a single calendar year
